findings.title: Planetarium view hotkeys swallow typing in the search field - object search by name is unusable from the keyboard
findings.what_happened: With the planetarium plan panel open and the caret blinking in the 'Search objects, names...' field, typing 'Vega' deterministically leaves 'Va' in the field: the 'e' toggled the ecliptic layer on and the 'g' toggled the equatorial grid on instead of entering text. Typing the full lowercase alphabet 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' left only 'abd' in the field - c/e/f/g/h/m/n/r are all bound to view actions (constellation lines, ecliptic, FOV overlay, grid, reset view, minimap, now) and after 'h' (reset view) the field lost focus entirely so i..z were dropped too. Reproduced at 30ms, 250ms, 400ms and 2000ms inter-key delays: it is a shortcut conflict, not a dropped-keystroke race.
findings.expected: A focused text field must consume ordinary character keys. Planetarium single-letter hotkeys should be suppressed whenever the primary focus is a text input (Flutter: check FocusManager.instance.primaryFocus?.context?.widget is EditableText, or move the shortcuts into a Shortcuts/Actions scope that a TextField's own shortcut scope shadows).
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > click the sidebar toggle (top right) > click the 'Search objects, names...' field > type Vega. Field shows 'Va'; the ecliptic line and the RA/Dec grid have both switched on behind the panel.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-11.png (grid + ecliptic appeared while typing 'Vega'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-18.png ('Va' after 400ms/char), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-19.png ('Va' after 2000ms/char), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-20.png ('abd' after typing the whole alphabet). Handler: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planetarium/planetarium_screen/actions.dart:507-624
findings.proposed_fix: In _handleKeyEvent, return KeyEventResult.ignored early when the primary focus is an editable text field, before the single-letter branches.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim on a fresh v-planetarium profile (site 40.00N/105.00W). Plan Tonight > Planetarium > sidebar toggle > click 'Search objects, names...' > type 'Vega' left literally 'Va' in the field, and the RA/Dec grid (labels +30/+15/0/-15, 3h..23h) plus the yellow ecliptic line both switched on behind the panel (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vp-09.png before, vp-10.png after). Clearing and typing 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' left exactly 'abd' (vp-12.png) - character for character what was reported. The focus-loss half of the claim also reproduced: after the alphabet run the field no longer had focus, and later keystrokes went to the sky (a stray 'h'/'r' recentred the view on the zenith, RA 5h48m = LST, Dec +40 = latitude). Code confirms the mechanism: planetarium_screen.dart:259-262 wraps the whole screen in Focus(autofocus:true, onKeyEvent:_handleKeyEvent), and _handleKeyEvent (actions.dart:507) returns KeyEventResult.handled for bare keyH/keyR/keyG/keyC/keyE/keyN/keyM/keyF with no test for whether primaryFocus is a text input, so the ancestor Focus eats KeyEvents that the TextField's IME text path never sees. Severity P1 is right: naming a target is the primary way into this screen and it cannot be typed. Cited location actions.dart:551-600 does contain the single-letter branches; the guard belongs at the top of _handleKeyEvent (actions.dart:507).

findings.title: Planetarium hotkeys are dead unless a text field has focus - clicking the sky never restores it

With the sky clicked and an object selected, 15 presses of '=' left FOV at 28.9 deg (should zoom in), and 'h' (reset view) left the view at RA 8h25m/FOV 28.9 deg instead of resetting to zenith/FOV 60. The same keys DID fire minutes earlier, while the search text field held focus.
findings.expected: Tapping the sky canvas should re-request focus for the planetarium Focus node so the documented shortcuts keep working; today only the initial autofocus works and the first click anywhere kills it permanently.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > click any star or empty sky > press '=' repeatedly, then 'h'. FOV readout at the bottom never changes.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-32.png (FOV 28.9 after 15x '='), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-33.png (FOV still 28.9 after 'h'). Source: Focus(autofocus:true, onKeyEvent:_handleKeyEvent) wraps a GestureDetector that never calls requestFocus - packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planetarium/planetarium_screen.dart:259-262
findings.proposed_fix: Give the Focus node a FocusNode and call node.requestFocus() from the sky GestureDetector's onTapDown; keep autofocus for first paint.

findings.title: Mouse-wheel zoom discards ~99% of scroll events - 172 notches move the FOV from 60 to 29 degrees
findings.what_happened: Each wheel notch is supposed to zoom 1.15-1.2x. Measured live: 5 notches spaced 2.0s apart took FOV 28.9 -> 14.4 deg (exactly 1.15^5, correct). 12 notches spaced 0.3s took 60.0 -> 41.7 deg (the effect of ~2.6 notches). 120 notches spaced 0.05s took 34.7 -> 28.9 deg (the effect of ~1.3 notches out of 120). Spinning the wheel at any natural speed therefore barely zooms; it took 172 notches over two minutes to get from the default 60 deg to 28.9 deg, and there is no other zoom control on the desktop layout (no +/- buttons, no FOV field, and the '=' / '-' hotkeys are dead - see the focus finding).
findings.expected: Successive wheel events must compound onto the pending zoom target, not restart the animation from the current (barely-moved) FOV. A user should reach an imaging FOV in a few flicks of the wheel.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > point at the sky > spin the wheel up 20 notches quickly, watch 'FOV (short axis)' in the bottom bar.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-28.png (41.7 after 12 notches), -29.png (34.7 after 40 more), -31.png (28.9 after 120 more), -36.png (14.4 after 5 slow notches). Source: _animateZoom sets _startFOV = current provider FOV and calls _zoomController.forward(from:0) on every event - packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/widgets/interactive_sky_view.dart:475-485,660-668
findings.proposed_fix: Accumulate into _targetFOV (use the in-flight target, not the current FOV, as the base) so N rapid notches equal N steps.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Measured myself. 20 xdotool wheel-up notches at 50 ms spacing over the sky canvas moved FOV 60.0 -> exactly 50.0, i.e. 60/1.2 - the effect of ONE notch out of twenty (95% discarded). Then 5 notches at 2.0 s spacing moved 50.0 -> 21.9, exactly the fully compounded 50/1.2^3/1.15^2 = 21.88, so slow notches apply in full. Code confirms the mechanism at the cited line: interactive_sky_view.dart:475 _animateZoom sets _startFOV from the provider's current (barely-moved) fieldOfView and calls _zoomController.forward(from: 0.0) at :484 on every scroll event (:660-668), restarting the 300 ms easeOutCubic instead of compounding onto the pending target. Location interactive_sky_view.dart:475 is exact. One sub-claim inside the finding is now false: the '=' / '-' hotkeys are NOT dead, so a working keyboard zoom exists - which is why I leave it at P2 rather than raising it.

findings.title: At a 1-degree imaging FOV the sky renders essentially empty - measured 1 star in 0.6 sq deg at astronomical dark
findings.what_happened: Zoomed to the minimum FOV (1.0 deg short axis), time set to tonight's astro dark via the TONIGHT button, view at the zenith (RA 17h44m, Dec +40, in Hercules): an 800x400 px patch of sky - 0.59 sq deg - contained ONE barely-visible dot (2 local maxima above grey level 40, zero above 60, on a background of 12). Star counts measured in the same pixel window while zooming out at the same sky centre: FOV 1.0 -> 1 star, 2.0 -> 6, 4.1 -> 33, 8.1 -> 74, 16.4 -> 328. Sky area scales as FOV^2, so surface density is flat at 1.7-3.5 stars/sq deg at every zoom - i.e. the depth never increases as you zoom in, and 2.9 stars/sq deg is exactly the whole bundled HYG catalog (119,600 stars over 41,253 sq deg), which is complete only to about mag 9.
findings.expected: An imaging-scale field is the whole point of a planetarium inside an astrophotography app - it is what you check framing and guide stars against. At 1 deg it should show tens of stars. The bundled catalog is the binding constraint, not the FOV-adaptive magnitude ramp, which the code intends to add up to +7 mag by 1 deg.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > wheel-zoom to FOV 1.0 deg > press TONIGHT in the time bar > look at the sky.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/fov1-night2.png (the empty 800x400 field), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/fovzoom-2.png .. fovzoom-16.png (counts above). Bundled catalog: apps/desktop/.../assets/planetarium/catalogs/stars-hyg-v1/tiles = 3,458,592 bytes over 768 tiles, ~28.7 bytes/star -> ~119,600 stars = full HYG.
findings.proposed_fix: Ship (or auto-fetch on first run) a Tycho-2-depth tileset, and set the HYG hand-off seam to HYG's real completeness (~9.0), not 11.5.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Symptom reproduced and the cause proved from the shipped catalog binary rather than from the app. TONIGHT set the clock to 2026-08-03 00:00 (astro dusk); scroll-zoomed to FOV 1.2 deg short axis centred on M57 (RA 18h53m35s, Dec +33d01'). The sky canvas covers 2.271 x 1.200 deg = 2.725 sq deg and contained 12 star blobs by an 8-connected >=3px detector on the raw capture (vp-24.png, vp-25.png) = 4.4 stars/sq deg. I then decoded the bundled pack myself: 768 NSPLNT01 tiles, 64-byte header + 16*lod_levels LOD index + 28-byte records {u32 id, u32 flags, f32 x,y,z unit vector, f32 mag, f32 B-V}; layout validated by recovering HIP 14135 = Menkar at RA 3h02m, Dec +4.09, mag 2.54. Total 119,432 stars = 2.90/sq deg whole sky, saturating at mag ~10 (N<=9 = 83,479; N<=12 = 117,930; N<=15 = 119,432), i.e. complete only to about mag 9 exactly as claimed. In the exact rendered footprint the pack holds 13 stars, faintest mag 9.0, with nothing fainter than 9.0 present at all. So the app draws 12 of the 13 stars it owns - the renderer is not dropping anything, the catalog is empty. A real Lyra field (b ~ +13) carries of order 100-200 stars/sq deg to mag 12, so the chart is ~30x too shallow at imaging scale, and layers_panel.dart:415-419 documents that no deep tileset is published, making mag ~9 a hard ceiling for a shipped user. One number needs correcting downward: the headline '1 star in 0.6 sq deg' is an unlucky patch - the honest density is ~3-5 stars/sq deg (2.90 whole-sky pack mean, 4.4 measured), so '1 star' overstates the emptiness by a factor of a few. P1 stands: framing and guide-star checks at imaging scale are a headline use of this screen.
findings.location_wrong: render_config.dart:434-489 does contain the FOV magnitude ramp, but that code is not the defect and editing it changes nothing on screen - at FOV 1.2 at astro dark it already reaches its 12.0 clamp, and the shipped pack has zero stars between mag 9.0 and 12.0 anywhere in this field. The finding's own 'expected' says the catalog is the binding constraint, yet the where still points at the ramp. Actionable sites: the bundled pack depth (apps/desktop/assets/planetarium/catalogs/stars-hyg-v1 + build_hyg_tiles), the deep-star tier (deep_star_providers.dart - showDeepStarsProvider default false, kDeepStarFovThresholdDegrees 8.0, kHygFaintFloorMag 11.5; layers_panel.dart:413-460; deep_star_catalog_card.dart:250 which asks the user for their own self-hosted base URL because no tileset is published), and the missing signal (star_catalog_fallback_banner.dart fires only when HYG is absent entirely, never when HYG's mag-9 floor is what is emptying the field).

findings.title: Layers panel claims stars brighter than mag 11.5 are available; the bundled catalog stops around mag 9
findings.what_happened: The Layers panel row 'Deep stars (Tycho-2 / Gaia tier)' reads 'No tileset installed - stars below mag 11.5 are unavailable', which tells the user everything brighter than 11.5 IS drawn. Measured on-screen star density is 2.9/sq deg at every zoom level, which is the entire bundled HYG catalog and corresponds to a limit near mag 9. The constant behind the string, kHygFaintFloorMag = 11.5, is documented as 'the bundled HYG catalog's faint floor' and is also used as minMagnitude when querying the deep-star store, so even after installing a tileset the 9-11.5 gap would never be filled.
findings.expected: State the real depth of what is installed (about mag 9) and set the merge seam there.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > Layers icon in the command bar > read the second row.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-30.png; density measurements in the previous finding. packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/providers/deep_star_providers.dart:25-28,91
findings.proposed_fix: Set kHygFaintFloorMag to HYG's actual completeness limit and reword the subtitle.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Already fixed. kHygFaintFloorMag is now 9.0 (deep_star_providers.dart:39, with a comment documenting the row counts) and the Layers panel interpolates the constant, so the live row reads 'No tileset installed - stars below mag 9.0 are unavailable' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2p-24.png). Because the same constant is the merge seam passed as minMagnitude at deep_star_providers.dart:105, the 9-to-11.5 hole is closed too. I independently counted the installed catalog (~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/catalogs/hyg_v42.csv, 119,626 rows): 41,149 at mag<=8, 83,124 at <=9, 107,938 at <=10, 115,518 at <=11 - the per-bin gain turns over after 9, so 9.0 is the correct completeness limit.

findings.title: Alt/az readouts ignore precession - stated positions are up to 1.4 degrees off
findings.what_happened: Clicking Capella at 18:38:16Z from 40N/105W/1650m the popup reported Alt 56.5, Az 295.7. Computing alt/az from the same J2000 RA/Dec with no precession gives 56.462/295.700 - an exact match; precessing to the equinox of date gives 56.804/295.681. Pollux at 18:39:17Z: app 76.0/214.0; J2000-direct 75.964/214.167; precessed 76.080/212.716 (1.45 deg of azimuth). So the horizontal transform uses J2000 coordinates unrotated, with no nutation, aberration or refraction either.
findings.expected: Apply precession (and ideally refraction) before the horizontal transform. 26 years from J2000 is already ~22 arcmin of position, and the azimuth error near the zenith reaches 1.4 deg, which is enough to mis-call a meridian-flip or an obstruction check.
findings.repro: Set the site to 40N 105W, open the planetarium at a known UTC, click Capella and Pollux, read 'Current Position'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-22.png (Capella: HYG118360, RA 5h16m40.7s Dec +45 59' 52", Alt 56.5 Az 295.7), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-24.png (Pollux: HIP37826, RA 7h45m17.7s Dec +28 1' 33", Alt 76.0 Az 214.0).
findings.proposed_fix: Precess catalogue J2000 coordinates to the observation epoch before computing hour angle.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with my own numbers. Clicked Vega at 2026-08-03 20:49:14 UTC from 40N/105W/1650m: popup reports RA 18h36m56.8s / Dec +38 47' 09" (J2000 to the arcsecond) and Alt 6.2 / Az 43.0. Computing alt/az from those unprecessed J2000 coordinates gives 6.2436 / 43.0466 - an exact match; precessing to the equinox of date (rigorous IAU 1976) gives 18h37m50s / +38 48' 36" whose alt/az is 6.1449 / 42.9005, which the app does NOT show. No refraction either - at alt 6.2 deg refraction is ~0.13 deg and the app shows the bare geometric value. Corroborating: AstronomyCalculations.precessFromJ2000ToDate exists at astronomy_calculations.dart:442 but a repo-wide grep finds ZERO call sites - it is dead code.
findings.location_wrong: Cited only 'packages/skotiq_planetarium (horizontal transform)'. Precise sites: the transform is equatorialToHorizontal at packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/astronomy_calculations.dart:262, and the unused precession routine it should compose with is precessFromJ2000ToDate at the same file :442.

findings.title: Moon is always drawn full and always labelled 'MOON 100%' - percent is fed into a 0-1 fraction and clamped
findings.what_happened: On 2026-08-02 14:26:36 UTC from 40N/105W the planetarium drew the Moon as a solid, fully-lit white disc with the label 'MOON 100%'. The true illuminated fraction at that instant is 84.6% (independent Meeus computation, elongation 133.7 deg), and the app's own Dashboard Moon card says 'Waning Gibbous 84% illuminated' while Plan Tonight's target card says 'Moon is 79% illuminated'. Three surfaces, three different numbers, and the planetarium's is the one that is impossible. Root cause is a unit mismatch: AstronomyCalculations.moonIllumination() returns a PERCENT (0-100) and its doc comment says so, but SkyRenderer._drawMoon documents its third tuple element as 'illuminated fraction (0 = new, 1 = full)' and does rawIllumination.clamp(0.0, 1.0). Any real phase above 1% therefore clamps to exactly 1.0, so both the terminator geometry and the label are pinned at full moon for 29 of every 29.5 days. Only within a few hours of new moon does the value fall below 1 and render anything else - and then it renders a 1%-lit crescent as if it were 100%-scaled.
findings.expected: The label should read the real illuminated percentage (84% here) and the disc should be drawn with the corresponding terminator, matching the Dashboard's Moon card.
findings.repro: Settings > Location > lat 40, lon -105 > Plan Tonight > Planetarium. The Moon glyph is near the default 0h/0deg view. Read its label; then compare with Dashboard > Moon card.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-10.png (full white disc, label 'MOON 100%'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-02.png (Dashboard: 'Waning Gibbous 84% illuminated'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-07.png (Plan Tonight: 'Moon is 79% illuminated'). Source: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/astronomy_calculations.dart:761-785 returns 0-100; packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/rendering/sky_renderer/solar_system_and_markers.dart:481-486 clamps to 0..1 and :571 does (illumination * 100).round().
findings.proposed_fix: Divide by 100 at the three call sites that build the moonPosition tuple (interactive_sky_view.dart:1026, planetarium_screen/actions.dart:212, widgets/view_controls.dart:396 - the exported finder chart is affected too), or better, change moonIllumination() to return a fraction and fix the one place that formats it as a percent.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live on the rebuilt bundle at 2026-08-03 20:43 UTC / 40N 105W: the chart draws a solid white disc labelled 'MOON 100%' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2p-08.png, again at v2p-21.png). My own Meeus computation gives 73.7% illuminated at that instant, and the app's own Dashboard Moon card says 'Waning Gibbous 74% illuminated' - so 74% is what the app computes elsewhere and 100% is the renderer's. Chain confirmed in code: astronomy_calculations.dart:844-868 moonIllumination returns (1+cos)/2*100 i.e. a PERCENT; interactive_sky_view.dart:1026 passes moonIllumination.illumination into the third tuple slot; solar_system_and_markers.dart:484-486 does rawIllumination.clamp(0.0,1.0) and :571 does (illumination*100).round(). Anything above 1% pins to 1.0.
findings.location_wrong: Cited solar_system_and_markers.dart:481 is the `if (moonPosition == null) return;` guard; the clamp is :484-486 and the label :571. The upstream unit error is at packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/widgets/interactive_sky_view.dart:1026, with the same feed duplicated in planetarium_screen/actions.dart:212 and widgets/view_controls.dart:396 - editing only :481 misses three call sites.

findings.title: 'Best Targets Tonight' transit times are computed for the night after tomorrow - every time is ~8 minutes wrong
findings.what_happened: On 2026-08-02 at 40N/105W the Tonight sidebar listed IC311 with transit 09:24 and NGC6685 with transit 00:48. Selecting each object shows its coordinates in the bottom bar: IC311 = RA 3h16m46s Dec +40d00', NGC6685 = RA 18h39m58s Dec +39d58'. The true meridian crossings for those coordinates at lon -105 are 09:32 / 00:57 tonight (2026-08-02) and 09:28 / 00:53 the next night. The app's numbers match neither - they match 2026-08-04 (09:24 / 00:49), i.e. two sidereal days of drift. Root cause: bestTargetsProvider passes imagingTime = twilight.astronomicalDusk as the 'date', and at this site astronomical dusk falls at 00:00-00:02 LOCAL, so its calendar day is already tomorrow; calculateObjectVisibility then builds its search window as DateTime(date.year, date.month, date.day, 12) + 24h, i.e. noon TOMORROW to noon the day after. Whether the list slips a day therefore depends on whether dusk lands before or after local midnight, which flips with longitude-within-timezone, DST and season - so the same code is right in winter and a day out in summer. The app also contradicts itself on the same screen: with NGC6685 selected, the sidebar's Info tab reports 'Transit 00:52' for the very object whose Best-Targets card two tabs away says 00:48.
findings.expected: The visibility window for 'tonight' should start at the local noon preceding the dusk being planned for (or simply take a night-start date, not a dusk timestamp). Transit for IC311 tonight is 09:32, not 09:24.
findings.repro: Settings > Location > lat 40, lon -105 > Plan Tonight > Planetarium > open the right sidebar > Tonight tab > scroll to 'Best Targets Tonight'. Note the transit time of a row, then click the row and read 'Center RA/Dec' in the bottom bar; compute the meridian crossing for that RA at that longitude.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-14.png (IC311 90 deg 09:24, NGC5311 19:58, NGC5313 19:59, IC4155 19:13, NGC6685 00:48), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-15.png (IC311 selected: Center RA 3h16m46s, Center Dec +40 00'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-16.png (NGC6685 selected: Center RA 18h39m58s, Center Dec +39 58'). Source: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/providers/planetarium_providers/mosaic_targets.dart:145-159 and astronomy_calculations.dart:1024-1025. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-17.png (Info tab for NGC6685: Transit 00:52) against rp2-14.png (Best Targets card for NGC6685: 00:48).
findings.proposed_fix: Pass currentDate (the night's date) rather than the dusk instant, or have calculateObjectVisibility anchor its window on the noon BEFORE the supplied instant (subtract 12h before truncating to the day).
findings.verdict_reasoning: The day-slip is real and I reproduced it deliberately, but the stated magnitude is wrong. Code unchanged: mosaic_targets.dart:145-149 passes imagingTime = twilight.astronomicalDusk as the visibility `date`, and astronomy_calculations.dart:1106-1107 builds the window as DateTime(date.year, date.month, date.day, 12) + 24 h, so whenever dusk lands after local midnight the window is the NEXT night. On today's date (2026-08-03) astro dusk shows 23:58, still calendar day Aug 3, and the list is CORRECT: IC311 09:24 and NGC6685 00:48 match my own transit computation for the Aug-3-noon window (13:24:15 and 04:48:52 UTC). I then set the planetarium date to Aug 2, 2026: astro dusk moves to 00:00 (calendar day Aug 3) and Best Targets STILL reports 09:24 / 00:48, whereas the correct values for the night of Aug 2 are 09:28 / 00:52 by my computation. That is the bug, reproduced. CORRECTION: the slip is ONE night, ~4 minutes, not 'the night after tomorrow' / '~8 minutes'. Severity lowered to P3 - a 4-minute transit error does not change which target you pick, and it only bites on nights where dusk crosses midnight.
findings.location_wrong: mosaic_targets.dart:146 is right for the caller. The other half a fixer must see is packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/astronomy_calculations.dart:1106-1107 (the localNoon/+24h window).

findings.title: 'Best Targets Tonight' ranks purely by transit altitude, so it recommends obscure galaxies that transit in daylight and pass through the zenith
findings.what_happened: The five 'Best Targets Tonight' on 2026-08-02 at 40N/105W were IC311, NGC5311, NGC5313, IC4155 and NGC6685 - all listed at '90 deg', with transit times 09:24, 19:58, 19:59, 19:13 and 00:48. The same panel, six rows above, states Sunset 22:16 and Sunrise 07:56 and Astro Dusk 00:00 / Astro Dawn 06:12. So four of the five 'best targets tonight' reach their best moment in broad daylight, and the panel says so on its own face. The tooltip is honest about why - 'Objects sorted by transit altitude (>30 deg)' - but that sort has two further consequences: (a) it is maximised at declination = latitude, so the whole list is objects that pass through the ZENITH, which is the one place a German equatorial cannot track through and an alt-az mount cannot slew through; (b) it ignores the Moon entirely, and the panel three rows above says the Moon is 84% Waning Gibbous, so five faint galaxies are the worst possible choice for this night. The app grades these targets itself and disagrees: selecting NGC6685 and opening the sidebar's Info tab shows a score badge of '20 - Poor', for an object the Tonight tab has just called one of the five best targets tonight. It is a magnitude 14.6 galaxy 0.9' x 0.7' across.
findings.expected: Rank by integration hours available inside astronomical darkness above a user altitude floor, then break ties with moon separation and object brightness/size. NINA's Sky Atlas and the ASIAIR both filter to the dark window by default; SGP's framing/target list at minimum shows the visible-hours bar. A minimum of: drop anything whose transit is outside the dark window, and show 'X.Xh above 30 deg in darkness' instead of a peak altitude that every dec-40 object shares.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > right sidebar > Tonight tab > scroll to 'Best Targets Tonight' and compare the transit times against the Evening/Morning Twilight table in the same panel.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-14.png (the five targets and their transit times), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-13.png (Moon: Waning Gibbous, Illumination 84%, and Sunrise 07:56 directly above), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-12.png (Sunset 22:16, Astro Dusk 00:00). Sort site: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/providers/planetarium_providers/mosaic_targets.dart:190-200 keeps everything with transitAltitude > 30 and sorts on transit altitude. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-17.png (Info tab for NGC6685: 'Mag 14.6', "0.9' x 0.7'", score badge '20 - Poor', Alt -4 deg).
findings.proposed_fix: Score on darkness-window integration time with a moon-separation penalty (the repo already has _scoreMoonDistance in planning/target_scoring.dart - reuse it), and surface hours-in-darkness rather than peak altitude.

findings.title: The command bar's 'Search' button (and its Ctrl/Cmd+K shortcut) never focuses the search field, and does not even switch the panel to the Search tab
findings.what_happened: With the right-hand plan panel already open on the Info tab, clicking the command bar's 'Search  ⌘K' button only showed a 'Search the sky' tooltip: the panel stayed on the Info tab and the caret was not placed in 'Search objects, names...'. Typing 'Albireo' immediately after produced nothing in the field. Selecting the Search tab by hand left the field still unfocused - typing 'Albireo' again produced nothing, the panel kept showing its 'Search for objects / Try "M42", "Andromeda Galaxy", or "Sirius"' empty state. Ctrl+K and Super+K also did nothing. Source: the handler is _openPlanPanelOnSearch, which on desktop sets _planPanelOpen = true and _layersPanelOpen = false and stops - it never selects the search tab and never requests focus for the text field.
findings.expected: A control labelled Search with a keyboard-shortcut badge should open the panel ON the search tab with the caret in the field, so the user can type immediately. Finding an object by name is the single most common thing anyone does in a planetarium; it currently takes three separate clicks (open panel, Search tab, click into the field) before the first keystroke.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > open the right sidebar and select any tab except Search > click the 'Search  ⌘K' button in the command bar > type 'Albireo'. Nothing is entered. Repeat after clicking the Search tab: still nothing.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-27.png (tooltip shown, panel unchanged), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-28.png (still on Info tab, field empty after typing 'Albireo'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-29.png (Search tab selected by hand, field still empty after typing 'Albireo'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-30.png (empty after Ctrl+K + 'M42'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-31.png (empty after Super+K + 'M42'). findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. findings.title: Object info popup keeps the old object's name and coordinates but recomputes Alt/Az for the NEW selection - it said Deneb was 'Below Horizon' while Deneb was 11.5 deg up
findings.what_happened: Clicked the star Deneb on the chart; the popup opened correctly (Deneb / HIP102098 / mag 1.3 / Star (A2Ia) / RA 20h 41m 25.9s / Dec +45d 16' 49" / Current Position 12.2 deg, Az 320.1 deg, badge 'Daylight'). Without closing it, I selected M57 from the search results. The view recentred on M57 (Center RA 18h53m35s, Dec +33d 01') and the selection ring moved, but the popup stayed open still headed 'Deneb' with Deneb's identifier, magnitude, spectral type and RA/Dec - while its 'Current Position' block changed to '-10.3 deg, Az 331.2 deg' with a red 'Below Horizon' badge. Independent computation for that instant (2026-08-02 14:51:01 UTC, 40N 105W): Deneb is at alt +11.46 deg, az 320.93 deg; M57 is at alt -10.33 deg, az 331.20 deg. The popup is therefore showing M57's horizon position under Deneb's name, to the 0.1 deg. It is not a one-frame race: 74 seconds later it still read Deneb / -10.4 deg / Az 331.4 deg, which again tracks M57 (-10.4 / 331.4) and not Deneb (+11.4 / 321.0). The popup also carries a 'Slew' button, so the object the user is reading about and the object the app considers selected are not the same thing at the moment they press it.
findings.expected: The popup must either follow the new selection wholesale or close. Half-following - identity and catalogue coordinates from object A, live altitude/azimuth and the 'Below Horizon' warning from object B - is the worst of the three, because the visible result is a true-looking sentence about the wrong star.
findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium. Click a bright star (Deneb) to open its info popup. Leave it open. In the right panel's Search tab type '6720' and click the M57 result. The popup still says Deneb but its Current Position row now reports M57's altitude and azimuth and flags 'Below Horizon'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-26.png (popup for Deneb: Alt 12.2, Az 320.1, 'Daylight'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-33.png (after selecting M57: view centred at RA 18h53m35s Dec +33 01', popup still headed Deneb, Alt -10.3 Az 331.2 'Below Horizon'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-34.png (74 s later: Deneb, -10.4, Az 331.4, still 'Below Horizon'). Computed truth at 14:51:01 UTC from 40N/105W: Deneb +11.46/320.93, M57 -10.33/331.20.
findings.proposed_fix: Bind the whole popup to one immutable object snapshot taken when it opens (and dismiss/replace it on selection change), instead of reading identity from a captured object and the live horizon block from selectedObjectProvider.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with a different object pair and checked against my own alt/az code, not the app's. Clicked a star on the chart: popup opened for HIP24951 (mag 6.5, A2V+, RA 5h20m39.2s, Dec +46d57'49"), Current Position 81.2 deg / Az 325.0 deg, badge 'Daylight' (vp-15.png). Without closing it I typed '6720' in the panel search and clicked the M57 result (vp-16.png, 2026-08-02 16:05:25 UTC): view recentred on RA 18h53m35s Dec +33d01', selection ring moved to M57, popup still read HIP24951 with all of HIP24951's catalogue data, but Current Position flipped to -15.5 deg / Az 346.2 deg with a red 'Below Horizon' badge. My independent GMST/LST spherical transform for that instant at 40N/105W: HIP24951 alt +81.19 az 324.67; M57 alt -15.54 az 346.31 (LST 5h50.5m vs the app footer's 05:50). Then a second instant in the opposite direction: pressing TONIGHT moved the clock to 2026-08-03 00:00:03 local (04:00:03 UTC) and the same stale popup, still headed HIP24951, showed Alt 75.0 / Az 112.4 with a GREEN 'Excellent' badge (vp-17.png) - computed truth M57 75.0/112.4, HIP24951 -2.8/4.5. So the app badged a star 2.8 deg below the horizon as an excellent target. Matching the other object to 0.1 deg in both directions, and surviving a time change, rules out any one-frame race.
findings.location_wrong: Symptom and file are right, but the finding omits the second half of the defect: the stale value lives in the SHELL, not the popup. object_info_popup.dart:476 (`final altAz = ref.watch(selectedObjectAltAzProvider)!`) is the read site; the field that goes stale is `_popupObject` (planetarium_screen.dart:101), written only on a sky tap (actions.dart:100-103), cleared in _dismissPopup (actions.dart:110-116) and passed to the popup at widgets/redesign/planetarium_shell.dart:303-306. A fixer who only touches object_info_popup.dart can make alt/az agree with the header while still leaving a popup describing an object that is no longer selected. One sub-claim is wrong: the finding says the Slew button targets a different object than the popup describes. It does not - _handleSlewToTarget, _sendToFraming, _addToSequencer and _addPopupObjectToTargetQueue all read `_popupObject` (actions.dart:141, 243, 266, 320, 327), so every action button acts on the object NAMED in the popup. Only the Current Position row and the observability badge come from the other object.

findings.title: Planets are computed for the equinox of date but stars and DSOs are drawn at J2000 - the two are mixed on one chart, so planets sit ~22 arcmin off the star background
findings.what_happened: Clicking Jupiter on the chart at 2026-08-02 15:12 UTC from 40N/105W gave RA 8h 39m 30.9s, Dec +18d 53' 53", Alt 38.1, Az 96.9. An independent Keplerian ephemeris puts Jupiter at J2000 RA 8h37m58.3s / +18d59'31"; precessing that to the equinox of date gives 8h39m29.5s / +18d53'50", which matches the app to 1.4 s of RA and 3 arcsec of declination, and its alt/az (38.11 / 96.94) matches the app's to 0.01 deg - whereas the J2000 position gives 38.46 / 97.12, which does not. So the planet path precesses. The star path does not: the app reports Deneb as 20h 41m 25.9s / +45d 16' 49", which is its J2000 position to the tenth of a second, and its Alt/Az reproduces from those unprecessed coordinates. Both sets of coordinates are then fed to the same projection, so every planet is drawn displaced from the true stellar background by the accumulated precession since J2000 - about 1m32s of RA and 5.7 arcmin of declination here, roughly 22 arcmin total, or two-thirds of a Moon diameter. The screenshot shows this in the worst possible place: Jupiter is drawn right next to M44, the Beehive, and the drawn Jupiter-M44 separation is wrong by that amount.
findings.expected: One reference frame for everything on the chart. Either precess the catalog to the epoch of observation before projecting (correct, and it also fixes the alt/az error already filed), or express the planetary ephemeris in J2000. Mixing them is worse than either.
findings.repro: Settings > Location 40N 105W > Plan Tonight > Planetarium > press the home/reset icon so the zenith is centred > click Jupiter and read its Coordinates, then click a bright star and read its Coordinates. The planet is equinox-of-date, the star is J2000.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-66.png (Jupiter: RA 8h 39m 30.9s, Dec +18 53' 53", Alt 38.1, Az 96.9, drawn beside 'M44 - Beehive'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-26.png (Deneb: RA 20h 41m 25.9s, Dec +45 16' 49" = J2000 exactly). Computation: J2000 Jupiter 8h37m58.3s/+18d59'31"; precessed 8h39m29.5s/+18d53'50"; alt/az from precessed 38.11/96.94 vs from J2000 38.46/97.12.
findings.proposed_fix: Precess catalogue positions to the observation epoch inside the render pipeline (a single rotation applied to the star/DSO arrays per frame or per minute), so planets, stars, the grid and the horizon transform all share one equinox.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced against an independent ephemeris. Clicked Saturn at 2026-08-03 20:51:39 UTC: app reports RA 0h58m00.4s / Dec +3 26' 07". My own Keplerian ephemeris (JPL approximate elements, light-time corrected) gives J2000 geocentric 0h56m56.9s / +3 19' 59" and equinox-of-date 0h58m19.2s / +3 28' 35". The app sits ~4.7 arcmin from the of-date value and ~20 arcmin from J2000 - unambiguously equinox of date (residual within the app's truncated-VSOP and my Keplerian error budget for Saturn). In the same session Vega read out at its exact J2000 position. So the two families are in different frames on one chart; the offset at Saturn is 82 s of RA plus 8.6 arcmin of Dec, ~22 arcmin, matching the claim. I also saw the exact scenario the finding describes - Jupiter drawn right beside M44 (v2p-26.png). Code: planetary_positions.dart:145-153 converts VSOP-of-date ecliptic coordinates with the obliquity OF DATE while the star catalogue is J2000 and precessFromJ2000ToDate is never called.
